Rules summary Goal Lose the fewest points . Game play 4 players recommended. Dealer leads 1st trick. Must follow suit if possible. Trick taker leads the next trick. Definitions Deal / Hand (noun): play of all cards. Trick : play of one card from each player. Taker : player who wins the trick. Contract : rule for scoring the deal. Declarer : dealer who selects a contract. Double : contract value ×2. Redouble : doubled contract value ×2 (total ×4). Business : two players with a double. Maximum : redouble all doubles and double any remaining players. Contracts Dealer selects the contract for the deal. Only the trumps contract is played with a trump suit. Contract scoring depends on the options selected: Contract scoring Default option Negative contracts Positive contracts Always played No tricks No ​♥ No Q No K♥ Last two Domino Trumps Scoring Deal Salade 2nd last last 1st 2nd 3rd 4th+ Basic 32 -1 /trick -1 / ​♥ -2 / Q -8 K♥ -3 -5 +20 +10 0 0 +2 /trick 36 52 -1 /trick -1 / ​♥ -3 / Q -12 K♥ -4 -8 +25 +15 +5 0 +3 /trick Wikipedia -2 /trick -2 / ​♥ -6 A♥ -6 / Q -20 K♥ -10 -20 +45 +20 +5 -5 +5 /trick Last two Last two tricks score negative points. Domino Extra hand where plays must be either: same rank as a played card, or same suit and one rank above or below a played card. A ⇨ play again. Must play, else pass. Taker can choose start suit in Domino Salade Extra hand with multiple contracts : no tricks, no ​♥ , no Q , no K♥ . Q♥ ⇨ -2( Q ) -1( ​♥ ) ⇨ -3 points (32 cards). K♥ ⇨ -8( K♥ ) -1( ​♥ ) ⇨ -9 points (32 cards). Anti-Salade Salade with positive score . Game mode Regular - 1 iteration Regular - 2 iterations Regular - 3 iterations Geronimo Each dealer deals once for every contract. Doubling After the dealer selects a contract, non-dealers may optionally choose to double any player(s). In positive games , non-dealers can only double the dealer. Non-dealers must double the dealer at least twice during the game for each dealer. Any doubled player may redouble. Between each pair of players (P₁ & P₂), where P₁ has a higher score than P₂: P₁ gains the difference between their scores ⇨ + (P₁ − P₂). P₂ loses the difference between their scores ⇨ − (P₁ − P₂). Redoubled: P₁ gains twice the difference between their scores ⇨ + 2×(P₁ − P₂). P₂ loses twice the difference between their scores ⇨ − 2×(P₁ − P₂). Trumps Dealer selects trump color. Must follow suit, else must play a trump , else must discard. Must play higher trumps Whenever a trump is played, each player must play a higher trump than those played before if possible. Must play trumps if cannot follow suit Must play a trump instead of discard if possible. Type of deck 52-card deck 32-card deck 36-card deck House Rules Can lead hearts Only when already played No ​♥ or No K♥ : cannot lead ​♥ until a ​♥ is discarded. Anywhen Anyone can lead ​♥ whenever they want. Take them all counts positive No Every trick counts negatively. Tricks only No tricks and Salade: positive scoring. Anti-Salade: negative scoring. Tricks and hearts No tricks, No ​♥ and Salade: positive scoring. Anti-Salade: negative scoring. Tricks, hearts and Queens No tricks, No ​♥ , No Q and Salade: positive scoring. Anti-Salade: negative scoring. Points scoring Basic scoring Will count scores with simple count (tricks score -1 each) Wikipedia scoring Will count scores as described in the English Wikipedia page of Barbu (tricks score -2 each, hearts -2, ace of hearts -6...) cards removed players 32 cards 52 cards 👤 3 players 7♦ 7♣ 2♦ 👤 5 players 7♦ 7♣ 2♦ 2♣

---

Barbu (or Barbuda) is a four-player trick-taking card game of French origin.  Each of the four players in turn becomes declarer.  The declarer picks one of seven contracts for each hand.  No contract is repeated until all seven have been played.   Many variants of Barbu are played which include different contracts and point schedules, but seven common contracts are:


    Barbu (don't take king of hearts)
    Hearts (don't take hearts)
    Last Two (don't take last two tricks)
    Nullo (don't take tricks)
    Queens (don't take queens)
    Trumps (take tricks)
    Fan Tan (be first out of cards)


See also Coup d'État, Dragonmaster and Guillotine.
See also The Dwarf King, Indulgence, and Phobos Infection: The Lost Journey of X27

I also have a problem with the inclusion of the game Fantan when all the other games are trick taking games. [Rating: 5/10] Overview: Compendium game in which five contracts are about avoiding tricks (don't get Queens, King of Hearts, Tricks, Last Two Tricks, and Hearts ), one about winning tricks with a set trump, and one about getting rid of ones cards first using a domino mechanism.  What I like: - Contracts bring a lot of different games into one game. - Deciding which contract to play by evaluating ones hand is always fun.
